title: Materials and chemicals sub-chain: wafers, photoresist, gases, wet chemicals, substrates and their supplier concentration
why_it_matters: SIA/BCG flag photoresist, specialty gases and wafers as chokepoints and SEMI sizes materials at USD 73bn, but firm-level shares and qualification lock-in are not yet evidenced.
questions: Which firms supply each major material category and what are their shares?
Where are materials produced vs consumed?
How long does it take a fab to qualify a new material supplier?
Which hidden intermediaries (purifiers, reclaim-wafer firms, chemical blenders) exist?
primary_sources: SEMI materials market reports and press releases
Shin-Etsu, SUMCO, GlobalWafers, Siltronic annual reports
JSR, TOK annual reports
Japan METI semiconductor strategy documents
EU Chips Act staff working document

title: Equipment segment map: tool categories, supplier concentration, and post-sale service economics
why_it_matters: Equipment is a USD 135bn market with single-supplier points (EUV) and a large post-sale service pool (~25% of ASML sales) that matter for both chokepoint and opportunity analysis.
questions: What are the main tool categories and who leads each?
How big is the service/spares/refurbished market?
What sub-suppliers (optics, lasers, vacuum, RF, ceramics, probe cards) sit beneath equipment OEMs?
primary_sources: ASML, Applied Materials, Lam Research, Tokyo Electron, KLA 10-K/annual reports
SEMI equipment market data releases
CSET semiconductor supply chain dataset (ETO chipexplorer)

title: Distribution channel: authorized distributors, brokers, e-commerce, and the direct vs distribution split
why_it_matters: Distributors sit between chipmakers and tens of thousands of OEM/EMS buyers, and the open-market broker channel is where counterfeits enter; the size of each channel is unknown.
questions: What share of chip sales goes through distribution vs direct?
How do authorized distributors earn money (margins, design-win registration, programming)?
How large is the independent/broker market and how is counterfeit risk managed?
primary_sources: Avnet, Arrow, WPG, WT Microelectronics annual reports
SIA anti-counterfeiting materials
US DoD / GAO counterfeit parts reports
ECIA industry data

title: Advanced packaging, substrates and test: who does it (foundries vs OSATs) and where
why_it_matters: AI chips shifted value into advanced packaging and test (test equipment +55% in 2025); foundries now compete with OSATs and substrates were a shortage item.
questions: Which firms provide 2.5D/3D and fan-out packaging and with what capacity?
Who makes IC substrates and how concentrated is supply?
How are wafer probe, final test and system-level test split between OSATs, test houses and IDMs?
primary_sources: ASE, Amkor, JCET annual reports
TSMC annual report (advanced packaging)
Ibiden, Unimicron annual reports
US CHIPS National Advanced Packaging Manufacturing Program documents

title: Custom silicon: hyperscaler/OEM in-house chip design, ASIC design-service houses and their relationship to foundries
why_it_matters: Cloud providers and system companies designing their own chips (AWS, Google, Microsoft) and turnkey houses (GUC) blur fabless/customer boundaries and create new intermediaries.
questions: Which system companies design their own chips and for which uses?
Which firms provide ASIC/turnkey services and how are they paid?
How are these firms tied to foundries (e.g. TSMC's 35% stake in GUC)?
primary_sources: AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure product documentation
Broadcom, Marvell, GUC, Alchip annual reports
TSMC Open Innovation Platform pages

title: Hidden intermediaries and support services: specialised logistics, fab construction, cleanroom, gas/chemical purification, reclaim wafers, probe cards
why_it_matters: The discovery pass found evidence of specialised purifiers (neon) and merchant mask shops but could not research logistics or other support services; these are likely overlooked niches.
questions: What specialised logistics exist for wafers, masks, hazardous materials and tools?
Who builds and equips fabs (EPC, cleanroom, sub-fab)?
What other small but critical intermediaries exist?
primary_sources: SEMI standards and market data
Company annual reports of logistics and fab-construction firms
Government supply-chain assessments (US Commerce, EU, Japan METI)

title: Current value-added and capacity shares by stage and region (post-2022), reconciling SIA/BCG and CSET
why_it_matters: The best stage-by-region value-added figures found are for 2019; capacity is shifting with CHIPS-type subsidies and the 2024 update could not be extracted.
questions: What are current value-added shares by stage and region?
How do SIA/BCG and CSET figures differ in definition?
What are current and projected wafer capacity shares by node and region?
primary_sources: SIA/BCG 2024 full report (PDF)
SEMI World Fab Forecast public summaries
CSET/ETO chip supply chain dataset
OECD semiconductor value chain reports
